{{Quote|I can't abide those Jawas! Disgusting creatures!|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]|<ref name="Episode IV: A New Hope" />}}
'''Jawas''' {{Pronounced|d͡ʒɑ:wə}}<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> were typically short [[Rodent/Legends|rodent]]-like<ref name="SSWOGS_">''[[Super Star Wars Official Game Secrets]]''</ref> natives of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. They were passionate [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]], seeking out technology for sale or trade in the deep deserts in their huge [[Sandcrawler/Legends|sandcrawler]] transports. A band of Jawas were responsible for locating [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and selling them to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] uncle, [[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]]. Another tribe of Jawas, led by [[Tteel Kkak]], found [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt's]] [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|rancor]]. They had a reputation for swindling, as they had a penchant for selling old equipment to [[Moisture farmer/Legends|moisture farmers]]. However, they were extremely passive beings, and hardly put up any resistance to colonists of their planet unlike other natives, like the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]], instead seeing foreigners as an excellent business opportunity.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Jawas-PM.png|thumb|left|180px|A pair of Jawas: one with an [[Ion blaster/Legends|ion blaster]] and another a [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolt]] remote]]
{{Quote|Utinni!|A commonly used Jawa cry|audio=Utinni.flac|<ref name="Episode IV: A New Hope" />}}
Jawas were easily identifiable by their traditional brown hooded robes, though it was not unheard of for them to wear other colors.<ref name="Slip">{{WEGCite|story=There's Many a Slip Betwixt Cup and Lip|book=Mos Eisley Adventure Set}}</ref> Other notable features included their glowing yellow eyes, small stature and high pitched, quickly spoken language<ref name="Episode IV: A New Hope" /> called [[Jawaese/Legends|Jawaese]].

Through the study of corpses and skeletal remains, [[Baobab family|Baobab]] xenobiologists discovered that Jawas appeared to be gaunt, rodent-like creatures, with shrunken faces and yellow eyes.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> Some research suggests that Jawas and [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]], two native species of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], evolved from the same extinct species, the [[Kumumgah/Legends|Kumumgah]],<ref name="Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref> while other research suggests that Jawas evolved from [[Human/Legends|humans]].<ref name="EP4NOVEL">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novel]]</ref> Furthermore, there is research suggesting that Jawas evolved from [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]].<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

At all times, Jawa faces remained obscured by a shroud of cloth to retain moisture, hide their identity and dissipate their body heat. Polished orange gemstones were embedded within the fabric to protect the Jawas' sensitive vision from the bright sunlight.<ref name="New Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> The only physical parts that were exposed were their hands, which had tufts of fur on the palms.<ref name="Droids for Sale">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/explore/visualguides/chp08.html|text=Visual Guide — Chapter 8: Droids for Sale}}</ref> Jawas were renowned for their incredibly potent odor. Repulsive to most species, this odor contained incredible amounts of information such as other Jawas' identity, health, clan lineage, last meal, maturity, arousal and even their mood.<ref name="Swap Meet: The Jawa's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Swap Meet: The Jawa's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref> Their odor was compounded by a mysterious solution Jawas dipped their clothes in to retain moisture, and their view of bathing as being a waste of precious water, which attracted swarms of insects to gather in the recesses of their hoods. Jawas evolved several important survival traits, such as exceptional night vision and a strong immune system. A Jawa's normal body temperature is 46°C (116°F) which resulted in a high metabolism and an efficient digestive system that drew all the needed nutrients from the Jawa staple diet of [[Hubba gourd/Legends|hubba gourd]].<ref name="Databank" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Sand stays. All else changes.|Iziz|<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Jawa_fortress.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A Jawa fortress in the desert hills.]]
Jawas were a communal, compulsive scavenger species who spent most of their life devoted to scavenging the deserts of Tatooine in search of any scrap metal, droid, or mechanical part left behind from millennia of star travel and technological advancement, where the dry climate of Tatooine preserved almost all debris. Most non-Jawas regarded the Jawas as scavengers and thieves, a description that most Jawas found pleasing.

The Jawa's unofficial motto was ''not to look for uses in a salvaged item, but rather to imagine someone else who might find a use for it''.<ref name="Swap Meet: The Jawa's Tale" /> And this was evidenced in their endless search for wares with which to trade with almost any being Jawas encountered. They had a kind of instinctive feel for machinery and electronics, notorious for knowing how to get a piece of equipment functioning just well enough to sell.

===Social organization===
{{Quote|Jawas&hellip; Never around when you need them.|[[Kyle Katarn]]|audio=Jawas.flac|<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Jawa_Leader_GH_by_Drew_Baker.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Jawa Clan-Chief]]
Jawas lived in separate clan families, each with distinct, separate territories for living and scavenging. Each Sandcrawler was led by a Clan-Chief, who was male. However, the overall operation of the Jawa clan was overseen by a female Shaman. A female Jawa became a shaman by either possessing some kind of [[The Force/Legends|Force]] ability with which to perform magic, overcoming an illness accompanied by a hallucinatory vision or was chosen and trained as the successor to the current Shaman.<ref name="Databank" /> The shamans were believed to possess the ability to foretell the future, and performed spells, hexes and blessings to protect the clan and ensure the well being of all clan members. This title gave them a great deal of respect throughout the clan, which was strange in the largely patriarchal Jawa society, and this allowed the shaman to assume a position where they were to be consulted upon, and asked often for their wisdom. With the important position within the society, the shaman did not travel in the sandcrawler and instead remained within the safety of the clan's fortress.<ref name="EGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> Other than shamans, females were shown little respect in Jawa society.<ref name="Card-SWGTCG-Jawa Shaman">{{SWGTCG|set=Champions of the Force (SWGTCG)|cardname=Jawa Shaman}}</ref>

The primary activity in a Jawa's life was scavenging and trading within their sandcrawler vehicles. Upon reaching adulthood, Jawas were chosen to work on their [[Sandcrawler/Legends|sandcrawlers]], and participate in the scavenger hunt, the search, trade and reselling of useful wares found within the deserts. All remaining Jawas lived within fortresses, nestled deep in the desert where their collected wares were stored, and Jawa children could be born and grow safely. The scavenging Jawas would return to their fortresses before Tatooine's storm season commenced.<ref name="Swap Meet: The Jawa's Tale" /> These fortresses had high walls made from large chunks of old wrecked spacecraft for protection against [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]], [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragons]] and Tatooine's sand storms.

[[File:JawaEngineer-SWGTCGAoD.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Jawas working to salvage a crashed [[X-34 landspeeder/Legends|X-34 landspeeder]]]]
Once a year, just before the storm season on Tatooine, all the Jawa clans would gather in the great basin of the [[Dune Sea/Legends|Dune Sea]] for the annual [[swap meet]]. Numerous sandcrawlers converged and the Jawas met to exchange their salvage. Other inter-clan business was also attended to such as the comparing of navigational data of the ever-changing desert and the arrangement of marriages to ensure cultural and genetic diversity.

Adhering to their scavenger instincts, it was quite common for different family clans to trade their sons and daughters for marriage through an intense barter or trade agreement.<ref name="Secrets of Tatooine">''[[Secrets of Tatooine]]''</ref> A common Jawa term for this was the trading of 'marriage merchandise'.<ref name="EGAS" /> Jawas found it acceptable to consummate their marriages in public.<ref name="Drawing the Maps of Peace: The Moisture Farmer's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Drawing the Maps of Peace: The Moisture Farmer's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>

===Language===
{{Main|Jawaese/Legends|Jawa Trade language}}
[[File:Jawaese-letters_Stop_that_Jawa.jpg|left|thumb|An example of written Jawaese]]
Jawas spoke [[Jawaese/Legends|Jawaese]], a randomly variable language<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> which was difficult to interpret due to its extremely high speech rate, and the Jawas' use of scent to add emphasis and tone to their words. To enable Jawas to more easily bargain and trade with other species, they relied on a simplified form of Jawaese, the [[Jawa Trade language]] which removed the use of scent in the language and was quite easily learned by species that commonly dealt with Jawa traders.<ref name="Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide" />

===Diet===
The Jawas enjoy eating [[Squill (creature)|squills]] for their tough, pungent meat. [[Mission to Tatooine (Luke Skywalker)|Once]], a Jawa clan took an Imperial transport capsule after it crash landed, and found Squills inside, happy to get a free dinner in addition to finding scrap.<ref name="TS">"[[Tatooine Sojourn]]"</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|The Jawas have a tendency to pick up anything that's not tied down, Luke, but remember, they're basically afraid of their own shadows.|[[Owen Lars/Legends|Owen Lars]] to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="EP4NOVEL" />}}
[[File:JawaNEGAS.jpg|300px|thumb|right|A pair of Jawas]]
The Jawas evolved from the [[Kumumgah/Legends|Kumumgah]],<ref name="Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide" /> who lived on Tatooine before the formation of the Galactic Republic and before Tatooine became a desert. During the [[Pre-Republic era]], sometime between [[25,793 BBY]]<ref name="DOTJFS1">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 1]]</ref> and [[25,200 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] punished<ref name="KOTOR" /> the Kumumgah<ref name="DOTJFS1" /> for defying their authority by [[Bombardment of Tatooine|unleashing an orbital bombardment]] that reduced the surface of the once lush world of Tatooine into little more than fused glass, which eventually crumbled and became desert sand.<ref name="KOTOR" /> Over time, the Kumumgah split into two races: the tall<ref name="Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide" /> Ghorfas, who would become the<ref name="LCT">{{StoryCite|story=The Lost City of Tatooine|book=Wikipedia:Dig_(magazine)|bformatted=''Archaeology's Dig'' July 1999}}</ref> [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]], and the short Jawas.<ref name="Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide" /> Analysis of ancient stone carvings found on numerous worlds, including [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and even [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], led scientists of the [[Imperial Archaeological Division/Legends|Imperial Archaeological Division]] in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] to propose the hypothesis that these carvings were of Jawa origin and that their race once traveled among the stars. It is not known whether further analysis proved their hypothesis to be true.<ref name="SWG:JWS">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=terminal|Explorer|Jawas Were Spacefarers!}} on Tatooine</ref> During the [[Jedi Civil War]], the Jawas spoke of themselves in a manner that suggested they are unrelated to Sand people and are also non-native to Tatooine. Whether this is truth or else a ploy to distance themselves from their more violent cousins is unknown. Also, due to the fact that the Sand People knew their history from generations-old oral narratives, it is debatable if the Jawas even knew of the story.<ref name="KOTOR" />

Due to the physically superior Ghorfas attacking Jawas and enslaving them, the less physically capable Jawas needed a place to be safe from attackers. At some point, following what was believed to be an important mining opportunity, the [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]] brought many sandcrawlers to Tatooine, though they abandoned the planet soon after they discovered the unstable nature of the local ores. Upon abandoning the planet, the sandcrawlers were quickly adopted by the Jawas, who would use them as mobile homes. The abandoned sandcrawlers radically changed Jawa civilization, serving as mobile fortresses against Ghorfas attacks and helped the Jawa lifestyle of tribes searching the deserts for materials to scavenge evolve. These vehicles served as a testament to the Jawa abilities of discovering unusual and unorthodox methods of making things work, and required continual maintenance to keep in working order.

As colonists settled Tatooine, the Jawas were not as hostile towards them as the Sand people were. In their newly acquired sandcrawlers, Jawas would tour the desert, picking up old droids or equipment left by moisture farmers and other settlers, and would then either sell them to any willing customer or trade them for something else. Sometimes, Jawas would steal things that caught their eye, leading to settlers to regard them as untrustworthy. Presumably, they used the money made from their dealings to acquire supplies or other necessities from the settlers or other Jawas.

[[File:Rontos-woswfg.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Jawas capturing wild [[Ronto/Legends|rontos]]]]
The Jawas also emigrated to other desert worlds, such as [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] and [[Florrum/Legends|Florrum]], and garbage planets, such as [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]], which was home to the [[Meeknu clan]].<ref name="Raxus Prime article">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20021024raxus|text=Raxus Prime}}</ref> Several were even seen on the planet [[Genon]] in the employment of [[Grappa (Hutt)|Grappa]], a [[Crime lord/Legends|Crime lord]], and several on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Another world where Jawas were present was [[Arcan IV]].

When the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Dass Jennir]] [[Mission to Orvax IV|traveled]] to [[Orvax IV]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] with the crew of the [[Uhumele]], two of his companions, who belonged to short sized species, disguised themselves as Jawas, implicating that they were not an unusual sight on this planet.<ref name="TPTN5">[[Dark Times 3|''Dark Times'' 3]]</ref>

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], a group of Jawas on Tatooine disabled R2-D2 and carried him off into their sandcrawler where C-3PO was also being held. The Jawas later sold the droids to Owen Lars. Afterwards, the Jawas were killed by Imperial Stormtroopers, and their bodies were burned out of respect by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]].<ref name="Episode IV: A New Hope" />

At [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], [[Tteel Kkak]], a Jawa sandcrawler captain, discovered a [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] during the salvage of [[Grizzid]]'s crashed ship, which he turned over to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]].<ref name="A Boy and His Monster: The Rancor Keeper's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=A Boy and His Monster: The Rancor Keeper's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

Sometime after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], a group of 480 Jawas was transported to [[Endor/Legends|Endor]] as part of a privately funded expedition to salvage valuable hardware from wreckage left there after the battle. They reportedly mutinied, forming a roving bandit gang that preyed upon any visitors to the moon.<ref name="Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide" />

In [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], some Jawas were forcefully taken to [[Skip 5]] on the [[Smuggler's Run/Legends|Smuggler's Run]] to help repair damaged [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] equipment.<ref name="TNR">''[[The New Rebellion]]''</ref>

==Equipment and technology==
[[File:Jawas_SWG1c130.jpg|thumb|right|175px|Red-eyed Jawas disembark from their sandcrawler]]
Jawas only rarely ever carried weapons due to their usual passive nature. However they did mostly rely on [[Ion blaster/Legends|ion blasters]] that shot beams of energy to disable droids, and [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolts]] for keeping them under control. Most Jawas also carried around various tools for repairing droids. They were also adept at creating custom droids, cobbled together from spare parts of other droids. These [[Monster droid/Legends|monster droids]], as they were called, could be specially designed for the specific needs of a customer.<ref name="NEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Jawas made their first appearance in the [[1976]] [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]]<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> of {{Film|IV}}.<ref name="Episode IV: A New Hope" />

===Conception===
[[George Lucas]] originally created a prototype of a Jawa that resembled a [[Wikipedia:Rat|rat]], though this was scrapped after he felt that it was too theatrical. The Jawas in ''A New Hope'' were played by twelve local [[Youngling|children]] including [[Gary Kurtz]]'s daughter, [[Tiffany L. Kurtz]], who portrayed the Jawa [[Dathcha]]. Their faces were covered by black stocking masks and wired on [[eye]] bulbs.<ref name="Much to Learn">{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-7-things-you-might-not-know-about-jawas|text=Much to Learn You Still Have: 7 Things You Might Not Know About Jawas}}</ref>

According to [[Stephen J. Sansweet]]'s book ''[[Star Wars: From Concept to Screen to Collectible]]'', the Jawas were the centerpiece in one of the strangest copyright infringement cases involving ''Star Wars''. In [[1978]], small hooded creatures with glowing eyes that [[Wikipedia:Neil Young|Neil Young]] called "Roadeyes" began accompanying the rocker on stage during a concert tour, in a tour film, and on the cover of the album [[Wikipedia:Rust Never Sleeps|''Rust Never Sleeps'']]. The case was settled out of court.<ref name="From Concept to Screen to Collectible">''[[Star Wars: From Concept to Screen to Collectible]]''</ref>

===Connections to other species===
[[File:JawaPod-SSW.png|thumb|left|250px| Jawas on pod vehicles scouting the Dune Sea as depicted in ''[[Super Star Wars]]'']]
No canonical source has revealed what a Jawa looks like under the hood. In behind-the-scenes shots from [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], the Jawas have squarish heads covered in black cloth with large yellow eyes that appear mechanical. However, this is a costume and so may not represent their canonical appearance. The original ''[[Star Wars]]'' novelization implies a possible familial relationship between Jawas and [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]]. It also describes Jawas as rodent-like and compares them to de-evolved Humans, though these could be mere metaphors.<ref name="EP4NOVEL" /> ''[[The Mystery of the Rebellious Robot]]'' calls them the "subHuman inhabitants of Tatooine,"<ref name="The Mystery of the Rebellious Robot">''[[The Mystery of the Rebellious Robot]]''</ref> and [[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary|''The Visual Dictionary'']] states that "their rodent-like faces are remarkably ugly."<ref name="Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' puts forth the theory that perhaps<ref name="KOTOR" /> the [[Kumumgah/Legends|Kumumgah]],<ref name="DOTJFS1" /> and the Jawas and the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] by extension,<ref name="Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide" /> are, in fact, [[Human/Legends|Human]], or at least are related to [[Zhell/Legends|them]]. During dialogue with the [[Unidentified Tusken Raider tribe (Jedi Civil War)|tribe]]'s [[The Storyteller (Sand People)|storyteller]] in the Sand People's village, if the main character, [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], asks whether the similarities between those who were taken by the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] and the Human colonists are physical or societal, [[HK-47]] will remark, "Cautionary: Master, if you mean to suggest that humanity is ancestrally linked to ancient Tatooine, you will strain his belief system to its pitiful [[Meatbag/Legends|meatbag]] maximum."<ref name="KOTOR" />

The Weavers' guild in the [[Wikipedia:Loom (video game)|Loom]] computer game, by [[Lucasfilm]], resembles Jawas.
